overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by omitting the date and time of posting from the Dec. 13, 2024 agenda for its Dec. 17 meeting, but found no other violation and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee failed to post proper notice for its Dec. 17, 2024 meeting, including a November 18 'Notice' with no topic list.
allegations.key_passage: To begin, we find that the document the Committee posted on November 18 entitled “notice” did not constitute a notice for purposes of the Open Meeting Law where it did not include any list of topics anticipated for discussion.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Dec. 13, 2024 agenda for the Dec. 17 meeting was not posted properly or timely.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the December 13 posting was properly and timely posted more than 48 hours prior to the meeting.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Dec. 13 agenda failed to record the date and time it was posted, as required for notices.
allegations.key_passage: However, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law where the December 13 posting did not include the date and time it was posted.

allegations.summary: Raised general concern about adding a 'Late Orders' item within 48 hours of the meeting, specifically the Dec. 16 supplemental motion on school closure.
allegations.key_passage: The late order in this instance related closely to the other topics already included on the notice regarding the closure of the Kennedy-Longfellow School and simply made clear that the Committee would consider taking a particular vote with respect to that topic.

remedy: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
